newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr/yen recoils but sets sights higher.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr/yen recoils but sets sights higher.

text.p: The dollar appears to have found a foothold above 113 yen and barring a near-term move below this threshold, the rate should begin a slow creep higher in the days to come, technical analysts said on Thursday.

"If we don't break lower by tomorrow I think you have to square your shorts and take another look," said Ture Johnson, technical analyst at Bank of America. "The longer it sits here above 113 the more likely it is that it will rally."
Many chartists who have been betting on a sharper slide in dollar/yen were revising their expectations on Thursday.
Solid support below the 113 threshold was holding fast, indicating that the downward drift in dollar/yen could be fading.

"In dollar/yen you have a lot of support between 113 and 112.75," said Ben Morden, technical analyst at I.D.E.A. Inc. "We died at 113 and I don't think there's a lot of selling interest at these levels."
Nevertheless, technicians foresaw only limited upside potential for the rate, with solid resistance lurking near 115 yen. They advised selling short on any move above 114.50 with stops above 115.
The dollar was also expected to adhere to a range against the mark between 1.7150, the low of the week, and 1.73, analysts said.
They advised selling the upper end of the range but said a decisive downturn in the rate is unlikely in the near-term.
"The daily and weekly studies in dollar/mark are supportive and until they turn bearish I don't think we're going to go lower," said Johnson.
